summary: A reply to David Walden's request in RFC 473 for MIX tools, passed along by UCSB. A graduate student reports having written a MIXAL assembler in SNOBOL4 and a MIX simulator in 360 assembler, with the assembler well debugged but costly to run and the simulator only partly debugged.

eli5.summary: A student answered a call for a pretend-computer program by saying he had written one, though it was not fully tested yet.

subtitle: A UCSB student reports a MIXAL assembler in SNOBOL4 and a partly debugged MIX simulator.

tldr.problem: David Walden had asked in RFC 473 who had assemblers or interpreters for Knuth's MIX computer.
tldr.mechanism: Mark Scott Johnson at UCSB replies that he wrote a MIXAL assembler in SNOBOL4 and a MIX simulator in 360 Assembler, and offers documentation, access information and source code.
tldr.outcome: The assembler is fairly well debugged and documented but expensive to run; the simulator is only partly debugged and has no documentation.

today: The status in the unit data is Unknown. The RFC is a historical reply, and RFC 494 later summarizes the responses to the query.

sections.title: A Reply to the MIX Query
sections.content: The RFC passes on a reply, written by a graduate student at UCSB, to David Walden's MIX query in RFC 473. Questions about "cheap" usage were to go to Roland F. Bryan at UCSB. The reply is dated March 18, 1973 and signed Mark Scott Johnson.
sections.eli5: A student answered a question from the network, and his teacher passed the answer on.

sections.title: The Assembler and the Simulator
sections.content:
Johnson wrote a MIXAL assembler and a MIX simulator the previous summer. The assembler is written in SNOBOL4, fairly well debugged and documented, but fairly expensive to run.

The simulator is written in 360 Assembler and only partially debugged. All instructions except I/O have been tested somewhat. Card reader input and printer output work, but disk files and magnetic tape simulation are not complete. It has no documentation, since it follows almost to the letter the specifications in Fundamental Algorithms.
sections.eli5: One program is nearly done but costs a lot to run. The other works for most things but is missing a few parts and has no instructions.

sections.title: Offer of Help
sections.content: Johnson offers to supply existing documentation, information on how to access the programs, and the source code. He hopes to finish the simulator the next quarter and says he will do his best to maintain and correct the programs if bugs are found.
sections.eli5: He says he will share the programs and try to fix any problems people find.

references.text: Walden, D., NWG/RFC 473, the MIX query this RFC answers.
